OBSERVATION
RCA complete. The pause-state writer still persists the retired vocabulary. Current code has src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:_decode_pause requiring doc['gated_mode'] == 'reconcile-check' and set_pause constructing {'gated_mode': 'reconcile-check', ...}. I reproduced in a scratch git repo outside the worktree: set_pause(... reason='maintenance' ...) wrote a gate blob whose raw JSON was {'gated_mode':'reconcile-check','paused':true,...}, and read_pause returned the same retired value.

HYPOTHESIS
The bug is a compatibility sentinel that was intentionally retained but also kept as the new-write value: _ref_lock.set_pause uses the legacy string directly instead of writing a current canonical gate/pause vocabulary, while _decode_pause only accepts that legacy string. Because both sides are coupled, the retired value continues to be produced indefinitely rather than being read-only migration compatibility.

CONFIRMATION
The deterministic scratch experiment confirmed the writer path without touching the checkout. Evidence that would have disproved this would be set_pause writing a current value while _decode_pause only accepted reconcile-check for old blobs; instead the new blob itself contains reconcile-check. Working comparison: mode/request retirement paths reject direct --mode reconcile-check while retaining narrow compatibility, but pause persistence still uses the legacy value on new writes.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION
Design-free fix-wave candidate: split write vocabulary from read compatibility. Make set_pause write a current sentinel, keep a narrow legacy decoder or migration for existing blobs, and add paired tests for old-read/new-write plus a fresh whole-tree sweep.
